@Joachim_Cor What’s your game about? Just a heads-up: even if the creator says it's ready, this model is honestly not good for a game engine. It’s basically a hollow shell that looks okay from a distance, but it's completely unusable for indoor scenes or close-ups. If you try to import it into Unreal Engine or Unity, you are going to face a massive headache trying to make it work.Also, you can actually make a model like this yourself using photogrammetry if you have a drone, or even a phone with a good LiDAR sensor (using Polycam). You'll get the raw textures and a general guide mesh, but you will still need to manually retopologize and clean it up in Blender.I'm pretty sure this specific model wasn't hand-made from scratch. The geometry just isn't accurate for a manual build. On top of that, it’s completely unoptimized: 405.6k quads with only 7 materials is a dead giveaway that a computer automatically converted a messy 817k triangle scan into quads. It will absolutely tank your game's performance. Anyone can make this easily by the ways i said.

Main Story Color Variants:
While they all share the same basic model, their colors indicate their "Level" or difficulty:
-Brown (Level 1): The standard, weakest variant encountered at the start of the game.
-Green (Level 2): Feature green skin with orange/brown stripes; they are more resilient than the brown type.
-Swamp Green: A rare, lighter variant with black spots, though similar in strength to standard types.
-Red (Level 5): Encountered late-game (near the Missile Silo). They are significantly more aggressive and have much higher health than brown or green variants.
-Blue (Ultra-Raptor): The strongest non-boss enemy in the game. They only appear if you achieve a 20+ kill combo without taking damage and then enter a new raptor-infested area. They are extremely fast, resistant to hit-stun from the machete or stun gun, and can kill the player in just one or two hits. 

Extra Crisis (Dino Duel) Variants:
Dino Duel mini-game introduces even more colors for mirrors or specific unlocks:
Yellow: A unique variant often associated with specific challenges or the Dino Colosseum.
Black/Alternate Blue: Used primarily to distinguish between Player 1 and Player 2 in versus mode.

Sarcofago a colonne con le imprese di Eracle, retro (inv. VC) — Arte romana, 160-170 d.C. Marmo asiatico. Altezza cm 100, larghezza cm 235; spessore cm 22. Il fregio con “alcuni gesti d’Hercole” è pertinente al retro di un sarcofago, di ignota provenienza, murato insieme al fronte ( inv. LXXIX ) nella facciata orientale della palazzina, la cd. Prospettiva, come ricordato da Montelatici. Era conosciuto dal Cinquecento, come risulta dai disegni di Giovanni Antonio Dosio e Guglielmo della Porta (Hülsen 1933, p. 24, tav. LXVII; Gramberg 1964, p. 34, n. 9). In un momento successivo entrambi i rilievi vennero spostati in un magazzino della Villa, dove rimasero fino al 1826, all’epoca dell’allestimento della nuova collezione nel Casino, depauperato dalla massiccia vendita delle opere a Napoleone Bonaparte: Evasio Gozzani ne predispose il restauro a opera di Massimiliano Laboureur o Antonio D’Este. Galleria Borghese, Sala 2. Scheda completa: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.13001567.

Coperchio di sarcofago con le vicende della nascita di Apollo e Artemide e loro ingresso sull’Olimpo, acroteri con personificazioni di Venti non pertinenti (inv. IVC) — Arte romana, ca. 150 d.C. Marmo di Luni. Altezza cm 34, larghezza cm 194. Di ignota provenienza, la fronte di coperchio di sarcofago è menzionata per la prima volta nel 1827 nell’elenco compilato dal Ministro Evasio Gozzani con le opere scelte per essere restaurate dallo scultore Antonio D’Este e collocate all’interno delle sale nel nuovo allestimento della Villa all’indomani della vendita della collezione archeologica da parte di Camillo Borghese al cognato Napoleone (B. 8097: Moreno, Sforzini 1987, p. 355). Nella guida alla collezione del Nibby il pezzo è posto sopra il retro del sarcofago con le imprese di Eracle (VC) nella sua attuale collocazione, in sala II (1832, pp. 75-76). The model *works,* but a few specifications.

1. the shaders are just the default blender soft shading. You can either remove then, and add the following-

"Diffuse BSDF > Shader to RGB > ColorRamp (constant) > MixRGB (Multiply) > Material Output"

And then plug the right texture into the other half of the Mix/Multiply node. (Via Image Texture node.)

Or you can buy a recreation of Genshin's specific shaders on ArtStation. (I think it's just $2 and incredibly well-made, if you want a more accurate, detailed shader)

2. He doesn't have any facial bones, other than his eyes, teeth (for some reason?) and I think eyebrows?

3. The Jabot is only on one side for some reason. You can go into the model modifiers for the two jabot pieces, and add a Mirror modifier to them.

4. All of the rig's bones are vertical for some reason

5. Doesn't have the ingame outlines. You can add this yourself like this;

-Go to the materials tab of the specific piece youre adding outlines to (you should do these one at a time. Annoying, I know.)

-Add a new material, and change the color to whatever you want the outline to be. (Genshin usually has a darker version of whatever color it's outlining.)

-Go to Settings under this new material, and enable Backface Culling

-Next to "Shadow Mode, click on Opaque, and set it to "none."

(This probably isnt necessary, but it keeps the lines from preventing light from hitting the model underneath)

-Go to modifiers, and add a solidify modifier. Set it's thickness to 0.01 with a 1.0 offset.

-Turn *off* 'Fill'

-Go to "normals" and click "Flip"

-Go to Materials, hover over Material Offset, and click the right arrow until youre at the material you want to be used for the lineart. (Probably "1" in this case.)

You can play with the settings from there. Up close, the lines *will* have random gaps in it. I'm not sure if there's a reasonable way to fix this without being too much effort to warrant it. It's a result of every single face being completely separate,,, for some reason.

Update on below comment.

Seems like this is the official model for MMD software, ported to Blender (probably with mmd tools?) and just re-released here. The lack of facial bones is because the MMD Tools addon has its own panel for that. Since it wasn't exported with MMD tools in the same way, you just cant control the face at all.
